goal.sl: Za glagolom in predlogom rabiš me, him, her, us in them (Jack knows her, with me), ločiš him od his in rečeš It's me.
goal.de: Du sagst me, him, her, us und them nach einem Verb und einer Präposition (Jack knows her, with me), hältst him und his auseinander und sagst It's me.
goal.it: Usi me, him, her, us e them dopo il verbo e la preposizione (Jack knows her, with me), distingui him da his e dici It's me.
goal.en: You can say me, him, her, us and them after a verb and a preposition (Jack knows her, with me), tell him from his, and say It's me.

say.sl: Za glagolom angleščina reče **me** (mene, me, mi) namesto **I**: **Can you help me?** (Mi lahko pomagaš?) **Mrs Birkett knows me.** (Gospa Birkett me pozna.) **you** ostane **you**: **I can see you.** (Vidim te.)
say.de: Nach einem Verb sagt Englisch **me** (mich, mir) statt **I**: **Can you help me?** (Kannst du mir helfen?) **Mrs Birkett knows me.** (Mrs Birkett kennt mich.) **you** bleibt **you**: **I can see you.** (Ich sehe dich.)
say.it: Dopo il verbo l'inglese dice **me** (mi, me) invece di **I**: **Can you help me?** (Mi puoi aiutare?) **Mrs Birkett knows me.** (Mrs Birkett mi conosce.) Il pronome va dopo il verbo, non prima. **you** resta **you**: **I can see you.** (Ti vedo.)
say.en: After a verb, English says **me** instead of **I**: **Can you help me?** **Mrs Birkett knows me.** **you** stays **you**: **I can see you.**

say.sl: Za **he** je predmet **him** (njega, ga, njemu, mu), za **she** pa **her** (njo, jo, njej, ji): **I know him.** (Poznam ga.) **Jack knows her.** (Jack jo pozna.) Zaimek stoji za glagolom, nikoli *I him know*. **her** je tudi svojilni (**her dog**: njen pes), **him** pa ni nikoli **his** (njegov).
say.de: Zu **he** ist das Objekt **him** (ihn, ihm), zu **she** ist es **her** (sie, ihr): **I know him.** (Ich kenne ihn.) **Jack knows her.** (Jack kennt sie.) **her** ist auch das Possessiv (**her dog**: ihr Hund), **him** aber nie **his** (sein).
say.it: Per **he** il complemento è **him** (lo, gli, lui), per **she** è **her** (la, le, lei): **I know him.** (Lo conosco.) **Jack knows her.** (Jack la conosce.) **her** è anche il possessivo (**her dog**: il suo cane), ma **him** non è mai **his** (suo).
say.en: For **he** the object is **him**, for **she** it is **her**: **I know him.** **Jack knows her.** **her** is the possessive too (**her dog**), but **him** is never **his**.

say.sl: **it** ostane **it** (ga, jo), **we** je **us** (nas, nam), **they** je **them** (njih, jih, njim, jim): **Can you help us?** (Nam lahko pomagaš?) **The sheep? I can see them.** (Vidim jih.) **it** in **them** sta tudi za stvari in živali: **The keys? I've got them.** (Ključi so pri meni.)
say.de: **it** bleibt **it** (es), **we** wird **us** (uns), **they** wird **them** (sie, ihnen): **Can you help us?** (Kannst du uns helfen?) **The sheep? I can see them.** (Ich sehe sie.) **it** und **them** auch für Dinge und Tiere: **The keys? I've got them.** (Die Schlüssel habe ich.)
say.it: **it** resta **it** (lo, la), **we** diventa **us** (ci, noi), **they** diventa **them** (li, le, loro): **Can you help us?** (Ci puoi aiutare?) **The sheep? I can see them.** (Le vedo.) **it** e **them** valgono anche per cose e animali: **The keys? I've got them.** (Le chiavi ce le ho io.)
say.en: **it** stays **it**, **we** becomes **us**, **they** becomes **them**: **Can you help us?** **The sheep? I can see them.** **it** and **them** are for things and animals too: **The keys? I've got them.**

say.sl: Tudi za predlogom je predmet: **with me** (z mano), **for him** (zanj), **next to her** (zraven nje), **to us** (k nam), **from them** (od njih). **Come with me!** (Pojdi z mano!) **This is for you.** (To je zate.) Z **give**: **Give me the key.** (Daj mi ključ.) **Give it to me.** (Daj mi ga.)
say.de: Auch nach einer Präposition steht das Objekt: **with me** (mit mir), **for him** (für ihn), **next to her** (neben ihr), **to us** (zu uns), **from them** (von ihnen). **Come with me!** (Komm mit mir!) **This is for you.** (Das ist für dich.) Mit **give**: **Give me the key.** (Gib mir den Schlüssel.) **Give it to me.** (Gib ihn mir.)
say.it: Anche dopo una preposizione c'è il complemento: **with me** (con me), **for him** (per lui), **next to her** (accanto a lei), **to us** (a noi), **from them** (da loro). **Come with me!** (Vieni con me!) **This is for you.** (Questo è per te.) Con **give**: **Give me the key.** (Dammi la chiave.) **Give it to me.** (Dammela.)
say.en: After a preposition, the object form too: **with me**, **for him**, **next to her**, **to us**, **from them**. **Come with me!** **This is for you.** With **give**: **Give me the key.** **Give it to me.**

say.sl: Osebek je pred glagolom, predmet za njim: **She likes him.** (Ona ima rada njega.) **He likes her.** (On ima rad njo.) Vrstni red pove, kdo je kdo. Žival z imenom je **him** ali **her**: **Meg? Jack loves her.** (Jack jo ima rad.) Za stvari pa **it**: **The bridge? I can see it.** (Vidim ga.)
say.de: Das Subjekt steht vor dem Verb, das Objekt danach: **She likes him.** (Sie mag ihn.) **He likes her.** (Er mag sie.) Die Stellung sagt, wer wer ist. Ein Haustier mit Namen ist **him** oder **her**: **Meg? Jack loves her.** (Jack liebt sie.) Für Dinge **it**: **The bridge? I can see it.** (Ich sehe sie.)
say.it: Il soggetto va prima del verbo, il complemento dopo: **She likes him.** (Lui le piace.) **He likes her.** (Lei gli piace.) L'ordine dice chi è chi. Un animale con un nome è **him** o **her**: **Meg? Jack loves her.** (Jack le vuole bene.) Per le cose **it**: **The bridge? I can see it.** (Lo vedo.)
say.en: The subject comes before the verb, the object after it: **She likes him.** **He likes her.** The order says who is who. A pet with a name is **him** or **her**: **Meg? Jack loves her.** A thing is **it**: **The bridge? I can see it.**

say.sl: Za **be** in samostojno rečeš **me**: **Who is it? — It's me!** (Kdo je? — Jaz sem!) **I love the fells. — Me too!** (Obožujem hribe. — Jaz tudi!) En zaimek je dovolj: **Jack? I know him.** (Poznam ga.), nikoli *I know him Jack*.
say.de: Nach **be** und allein sagst du **me**: **Who is it? — It's me!** (Wer ist da? — Ich bin's!) **I love the fells. — Me too!** (Ich liebe die Berge. — Ich auch!) Ein Pronomen reicht: **Jack? I know him.** (Den kenne ich.), nie *I know him Jack*.
say.it: Dopo **be** e da solo dici **me**: **Who is it? — It's me!** (Chi è? — Sono io!) **I love the fells. — Me too!** (Adoro i monti. — Anch'io!) Basta un pronome: **Jack? I know him.** (Lo conosco.), mai *I know him Jack*, anche se in italiano si dice *lo conosco, Jack*.
say.en: After **be**, and alone, say **me**: **Who is it? — It's me!** **I love the fells. — Me too!** One pronoun is enough: **Jack? I know him.** (never *I know him Jack.*)

Granny Maggie and Auntie Edna are by the fire, and Old Wilf sits with ___ (they). Jack comes in with Meg, and the children run to ___ (she). — Can you help ___ (I), Jack? translation.sl: V gostilni Packhorse je petek zvečer. Gospod Dixon je pri točilnem pultu in gospa Birkett mu prinese skodelico čaja. Babica Maggie in teta Edna sta pri ognju, stari Wilf pa sedi z njima. Jack pride z Meg in otroci stečejo k njej. — Mi lahko pomagaš, Jack? Pladenj je težak. — Seveda! Daj mi ga. — Hvala, srček. Ta scone je zate. Pridi, sedi k nam!
translation.de: Es ist Freitagabend im Gasthaus Packhorse. Mr Dixon ist an der Theke, und Mrs Birkett bringt ihm eine Tasse Tee. Oma Maggie und Tante Edna sitzen am Feuer, und der alte Wilf sitzt bei ihnen. Jack kommt mit Meg herein, und die Kinder laufen zu ihr. — Kannst du mir helfen, Jack? Das Tablett ist schwer. — Klar! Gib es mir. — Danke, Schatz. Dieser Scone ist für dich. Komm, setz dich zu uns!
translation.it: È venerdì sera alla locanda Packhorse. Il signor Dixon è al bancone e Mrs Birkett gli porta una tazza di tè. Nonna Maggie e zia Edna sono vicino al fuoco, e il vecchio Wilf siede con loro. Jack entra con Meg e i bambini corrono da lei. — Mi aiuti, Jack? Il vassoio è pesante. — Certo! Dallo a me. — Grazie, tesoro. Questo scone è per te. Vieni a sederti con noi!
translation.en: It's Friday night at the Packhorse Inn. Mr Dixon is at the bar, and Mrs Birkett brings him a cup of tea. Granny Maggie and Auntie Edna are by the fire, and Old Wilf sits with them. Jack comes in with Meg, and the children run to her. — Can you help me, Jack? The tray is heavy. — Of course! Give it to me. — Thank you, love. This scone is for you. Come and sit with us!

exercises.text: Mrs Hartley is at the school gate. The children wave to ___ (she), and she smiles at ___ (they). Mr Tyson comes with Alfie. — Good morning, Mr Tyson! Can I talk to ___ (you)? — Of course. Alfie, wait for ___ (I) here. — Alfie is a good boy; I like ___ (he). — Thank you! Come and see ___ (we) at the mill.

translation.sl: Gospa Hartley je pri šolskih vratih. Otroci ji mahajo, ona pa se jim nasmehne. Gospod Tyson pride z Alfiejem. — Dobro jutro, gospod Tyson! Lahko govorim z vami? — Seveda. Alfie, počakaj me tukaj. — Alfie je priden fant, rada ga imam. — Hvala! Pridite k nam v mlin.
translation.de: Mrs Hartley steht am Schultor. Die Kinder winken ihr zu, und sie lächelt sie an. Mr Tyson kommt mit Alfie. — Guten Morgen, Mr Tyson! Kann ich mit Ihnen sprechen? — Natürlich. Alfie, warte hier auf mich. — Alfie ist ein lieber Junge, ich mag ihn. — Danke! Besuchen Sie uns in der Mühle.
translation.it: Mrs Hartley è al cancello della scuola. I bambini la salutano con la mano e lei sorride loro. Il signor Tyson arriva con Alfie. — Buongiorno, signor Tyson! Posso parlarle? — Certo. Alfie, aspettami qui. — Alfie è un bravo bambino, gli voglio bene. — Grazie! Venga a trovarci al mulino.
translation.en: Mrs Hartley is at the school gate. The children wave to her, and she smiles at them. Mr Tyson comes with Alfie. — Good morning, Mr Tyson! Can I talk to you? — Of course. Alfie, wait for me here. — Alfie is a good boy; I like him. — Thank you! Come and see us at the mill.
